claims.text: Alerting rules sit in rule groups beside recording rules and are evaluated with them at the evaluation interval (15 s on staging); each result series of the expression is an alert.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Configuration > Alerting rules and Recording rules (rule groups); prometheus.yaml evaluation_interval: 15s at stage-4

claims.text: An alert is pending while the expression returns it and firing once it has returned it for the rule's `for` duration; if the result disappears while pending, the alert is dropped and `for` starts again; a firing alert resolves when the result disappears.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Alerting rules: 'for' clause, pending and firing states

claims.text: A PromQL comparison without `bool` (e.g. `> 0.0672`) filters: it keeps only series for which it holds. `and` returns left-hand series that have a series with exactly matching labels on the right; both recorded shares carry only `job`.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Querying > Operators: comparison binary operators, logical/set binary operators; slo.rules.yml sum by (job) lines 14-21

claims.text: Rule `labels` are added to the alert; Prometheus gives a label such as `severity` no meaning of its own. `annotations` hold informational text carried with the alert (here `summary` and `runbook`).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Alerting rules: labels and annotations

claims.text: alerts.md: `page` calls the person on duty at once (on-call.md); `ticket` becomes a backlog task handled in working hours; each `page` alert has a file of first steps named by the `runbook` annotation.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/alerts.md lines 62-65 at stage-4

claims.text: Prometheus keeps alert states (pending, firing) but sends no notification to anyone; staging runs no component that sends them at stage-4.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/alerts.md lines 83-85 at stage-4; Prometheus docs, Alerting overview (notifications are sent by a separate Alertmanager)

claims.text: promtool test input: `interval` is the spacing of samples; `a+bxn` starts at a and adds b for each of the next n samples (n+1 values); `axn` repeats a; values separated by spaces follow one another.

claims.text: alert_rule_test compares the alerts firing at eval_time under its alertname with exp_alerts; `exp_alerts: []` expects no alert of that name firing, and any difference fails the test. exp_labels hold the series' labels left by the expression plus the rule's labels.
